question: Is there an independent rule that establishes flow-regime eligibility for UNINSPECTED Lewis runs, using neither CFD agreement, nor measured-versus-predicted divergence, nor any PhysMAP outcome?
searched: Lewis's remaining documentation first -- Section 7.2 (the only regime section), the Chapter 2 stability review, and Appendix E -- then outward.

metais_eckert_1964.what: Convection regime diagram for vertical tubes; Re versus Gr*Pr*d/L, with forced, combined, transition and turbulent regions.
metais_eckert_1964.data_available: YES, and at the right basis. Lewis's Table E.4 gives Gr*Pr*d/L at mean film for 29 of 30 runs, and Aung (1987) specifies mean film, so the basis is fixed by an external citation rather than by us.
why_it_is_rejected: Lewis reports that Barozzi et al (1984) found the diagram UNRELIABLE for estimating the effect of natural convection on laminar forced convection FOR WATER FLOWING UPWARD IN A UNIFORMLY HEATED VERTICAL TUBE -- exactly this configuration. We have this only through Lewis's one-sentence report and cannot check which boundary was tested.
Lewis notes the diagram's limits 'have not been reviewed in the light of more recently obtained data'.

Lewis's own partial validation of the boundaries is explicitly 'cursory', and he reached it by examining his measured data AND his numerical predictions -- so his endorsement is built from precisely the evidence this rule may not use.

He states the plotted positions are 'very sensitive to the choice of reference temperature', and that on the inlet-bulk basis 'the majority of the points lay in the laminar forced convection regime' -- a different answer.

petukhov_1969.what: x*_tr = 12.9 * C * (Gr_q/Re)^-0.8, C = 1 with a calming section and C = 1 + 10*exp(-0.0025*Re) without one. Measured on UPFLOW OF WATER with uniform heat flux, using wall temperature fluctuations to detect instability onset -- the same detection method Lewis used, in the same configuration.
petukhov_1969.applied: Predicts transition at x/d between 170 and 6500 for Lewis's runs. The tube is 159.66 diameters. So it predicts NO transition anywhere, in any run.
why_it_is_rejected: That contradicts Lewis's direct observation of wall temperature fluctuations, which is source-reported flow behaviour and not an agreement measure.
Their stated data range is 10^3 < Gr_q/Re < 4e5 and 250 < Re. Only 6 of 30 Lewis runs fall inside it on the inlet-bulk basis.

Most Lewis runs sit BELOW the lower Gr_q/Re bound, and with a -0.8 exponent that extrapolation pushes the transition distance further away -- the PERMISSIVE direction. It would return 'laminar' almost by construction, which is the same failure that disqualified Hallman's criterion.
petukhov_1969.verdict: REJECTED. Same failure mode as Hallman: permissive extrapolation outside the calibrated range, contradicted by direct observation.

yao_1987a.what: Linear stability analysis of fully-developed buoyancy-aided flow in a vertical pipe at uniform heat flux (Int. J. Heat Mass Transfer 30(4):707-716). The flow CAN become unstable for Gr_q/Re > 300 and Re > 80. Below the boundary it is a STABILITY statement, which is the direction eligibility needs.
yao_1987a.why_it_is_the_strongest: It is an analysis, not a correlation fitted to data, so the 'outside its calibration range' objection that killed Hallman and Petukhov does not apply in the same way. Its configuration matches exactly. It is conservative: it flags possible instability, so using it to EXCLUDE is the safe direction.
yao_1987a.the_problem: Yao's analysis is CONSTANT-property. Lewis's water is not -- viscosity falls by a factor of 2.1 across the tube. Mapping the experiment onto Yao's single parameter needs a reference temperature that a constant-property analysis cannot supply.

basis_robustness_test.method: Evaluate the verdict on all three of Lewis's own bases (Tables E.2, E.3, E.4) and keep only runs whose verdict is the same on all three.

yao_1987a.verdict: APPLICABLE, but it yields too few runs. Three are stable on every basis -- 16A, 20A and 26A -- and 16A is a SPENT development run. Two remain.

conclusion.finding: Lewis cannot support an independent eligibility rule that yields a scoreable set.
conclusion.arithmetic: The only admissible criterion leaves 2 usable runs after the spent ones are removed. Two runs are two cases. Axial stations are not cases, so there is no arithmetic that turns this into an evaluation set.
conclusion.and_worse: Both survivors -- 20A and 26A -- have local Nu only in Figures 6.13 and 6.12, so they would need digitisation; and 20A is the run the digitiser already REJECTED (one marker recovered, implied Prandtl number 0.15 instead of ~8).
conclusion.disposition: Lewis is RETAINED as a reproducible causal demonstration -- it has the richest per-run conditions of anything reachable, its property laws are published, and the variable-property rebuild now matches Lewis's own laminar prediction to about 5%. It is NOT the scored validation source.
conclusion.next: A different source is required for scored validation. Barozzi (1993) is open and has the strongest steadiness evidence found, but is horizontal -- a different mechanism -- so it is a separate generalization vehicle, not a substitute.

not_used: No CFD result, no measured-versus-predicted divergence, and no PhysMAP output entered any judgement on this page. The rules were stated with their published validity limits, then applied.
